subject: history_social
passage: In 1976 the Hōkūleʻa, a double-hulled voyaging canoe built by the Polynesian Voyaging Society, sailed about 4,000 kilometers from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti. Its course was set by Mau Piailug, a master navigator from Micronesia who read the rising and setting points of stars, the direction of ocean swells, and the flight of seabirds. Neither a magnetic compass nor modern navigational charts ______ used to guide the canoe, and the voyage strengthened the case that ancient Polynesians had deliberately navigated such distances rather than drifting to new islands by chance.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: When two subjects are joined by "neither ... nor," the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Here the closer subject is "modern navigational charts," which is plural, and the passage is set in the past, so the verb must be the plural past form "were."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Has been" is singular, so it doesn't agree with the nearer subject, the plural "charts."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Is" is singular, so it doesn't agree with the plural "charts," and it is also in the present tense.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Was" agrees with the farther subject, "a magnetic compass," but with "neither ... nor" the verb must agree with the nearer subject, the plural "charts."
explanation.D: Correct. The plural past-tense verb "were" agrees with the nearer subject, "modern navigational charts," and fits the 1976 setting.
